_readme: Round 1 of 7 — big august 9th batch (in-copyright PDFs). 24 of 25 books processed; Atomic Habits excluded (PDF extraction yielded only ~5K chars, insufficient to ground a synopsis — flagged for retry). Synopses grounded in real detect.mjs-extracted text; mentions curated from candidates.json per docs/detector.md exclusion rules; genres per tools/genres.mjs.

books.author: David McCullough
books.synopsis: Narrative history of the year 1776, following George Washington and the Continental Army from the siege of Boston through the disastrous defense of New York, the retreat across New Jersey, and the crossing of the Delaware to the counterstrokes at Trenton and Princeton.

books.title: 21 Lessons for the 21st Century
books.author: Yuval Noah Harari
books.synopsis: A collection of essays on how technological disruption, biotechnology, and artificial intelligence are undermining the political and religious stories that structured twentieth-century life, covering topics from work and data to nationalism, immigration, terrorism, and post-truth politics.

books.title: A Little Life
books.author: Hanya Yanagihara
books.synopsis: Four college friends—Willem, JB, Malcolm, and Jude—build careers and share an apartment in New York, and the novel widens over decades into the backstory of Jude St. Francis, a lawyer whose ruined legs, scarred body, and secret cutting trace back to abuse by Brother Luke at a monastery and years of exploitation before he was taken in by his law professor Harold.

books.title: A Mercy
books.author: Toni Morrison
books.synopsis: In 1680s colonial Virginia, the trader Jacob Vaark takes in Florens, an enslaved girl offered to him by her mother in payment of a debt, to join the household of women bound to his remote farm. Told in shifting first-person voices, the novel traces how Jacob's death from smallpox and the fragile bonds among these women unravel the household, while Florens searches for the free black blacksmith she loves.

books.title: A People's History of the United States
books.author: Howard Zinn
books.synopsis: A narrative history of the United States running from Columbus's 1492 landing through the 2000 election, told deliberately from the standpoint of Arawaks, indentured servants and slaves, industrial workers, immigrants, women, and dissenters rather than the 'Founding Fathers,' generals, and presidents who usually anchor textbook accounts.

books.title: A Raisin in the Sun
books.author: Lorraine Hansberry
books.synopsis: The Younger family in 1950s Chicago clashes over what to do with a $10,000 life-insurance check, as son Walter's dream of a liquor-store investment collides with his mother's plan to buy a house in the white neighborhood of Clybourne Park.

books.title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
books.author: Bill Bryson
books.synopsis: Bryson traces how scientists pieced together the history of the universe, the Earth, and life itself, from Darwin's On the Origin of Species through geology, chemistry, and paleontology, dwelling on the eccentric, often overlooked people who made the discoveries.

books.title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
books.author: Khaled Hosseini
books.synopsis: Mariam, an illegitimate girl married off to the abusive shoemaker Rasheed, and Laila, a younger neighbor forced into the same marriage after losing her family and her love Tariq to war, forge a fierce bond as they endure decades of violence and upheaval in Kabul.

books.title: A Walk to Remember
books.author: Nicholas Sparks
books.synopsis: In 1958 Beaufort, North Carolina, minister's daughter Jamie Sullivan draws reluctant high school senior Landon Carter into her Christmas play and her Bible readings, and he falls for her as she conceals that she is dying of leukemia.

books.title: A Man Called Ove
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.synopsis: Ove, a rigid fifty-nine-year-old widower obsessed with rules and his Saab, keeps having his repeated suicide attempts interrupted by a pregnant new neighbor, her family, and a stray cat that gradually pull him back into life.

books.title: A Walk in the Woods: Rediscovering America on the Appalachian Trail
books.author: Bill Bryson
books.synopsis: A middle-aged travel writer resolves to hike all 2,100-plus miles of the Appalachian Trail from Georgia to Maine with his out-of-shape, recovering-alcoholic old friend Katz, and the two stumble through blizzards, bears, exhaustion, and the trail's oddball hikers and towns while never quite making it the whole way.

books.title: Alias Grace
books.author: Margaret Atwood
books.synopsis: A convicted servant-girl in 1850s Canada, imprisoned since sixteen for the axe-murder of her employer and his housekeeper-mistress, is interviewed by a young doctor probing her patchy, contradictory memories of the killings while she recalls her immigrant childhood and the fatal household she worked in before the crime.

books.title: All the Light We Cannot See
books.author: Anthony Doerr
books.synopsis: A blind French girl hides in her great-uncle's house in besieged Saint-Malo with a legendary cursed diamond, while a German orphan boy conscripted into the Wehrmacht for his gift with radios is sent to hunt the Resistance transmission she depends on, their paths converging as Allied bombs fall on the walled city in August 1944.

books.title: All the Pretty Horses
books.author: Cormac McCarthy
books.synopsis: After his grandfather's death and the loss of the family ranch, teenage John Grady Cole leaves West Texas on horseback with his friend Rawlins, crossing into Mexico where a runaway boy named Blevins draws them into trouble with the rurales and John Grady falls for the daughter of a wealthy hacienda owner.

books.title: American Pastoral
books.author: Philip Roth
books.synopsis: Narrator Nathan Zuckerman reconstructs the life of Seymour 'Swede' Levov, the golden athlete of Weequahic's Jewish community who inherits his father's Newark glove factory and builds a seemingly ideal life, only to have it shattered when his stuttering teenage daughter Merry bombs the local general store and post office in protest of the Vietnam War, killing a man and vanishing underground.

books.title: Anathem
books.author: Neal Stephenson
books.synopsis: On the planet Arbre, a young monk-like scholar cloistered in a walled mathematical community is drawn out into the wider world when an alien starship enters orbit, forcing the secular authorities and the sequestered orders of philosophers to confront a threat neither can handle alone.

books.title: And Then There Were None
books.author: Agatha Christie
books.synopsis: Ten strangers, each secretly guilty of a death they've escaped punishment for, are lured to an isolated island off the Devon coast, where an unseen accuser broadcasts their crimes and murders them one by one in the pattern of an old nursery rhyme.

books.title: Angela's Ashes
books.author: Frank McCourt
books.synopsis: A memoir of a childhood spent in Depression-era Brooklyn and then Limerick, Ireland, where poverty, a drunken father, dead infant siblings, and a devoutly Catholic upbringing shape a boy's slow, resourceful climb toward escaping back to America.

books.title: Angels & Demons
books.author: Dan Brown
books.synopsis: After a CERN physicist is branded with an ambigram and murdered, Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon and physicist Vittoria Vetra race across Rome to stop the resurrected Illuminati from detonating stolen antimatter beneath the Vatican during a papal conclave.

books.title: Another Country
books.author: James Baldwin
books.synopsis: A Black jazz musician in New York self-destructs through an abusive affair with a white woman and jumps off the George Washington Bridge, and his death exposes the tangled, interracial, and bisexual relationships among the friends and sister he leaves behind in Greenwich Village and beyond.

books.title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
books.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
books.synopsis: A concise tour through modern astrophysics, from the Big Bang and the formation of matter through dark matter, dark energy, the electromagnetic spectrum, and the planets of the solar system, closing with reflections on humanity's cosmic perspective.

books.title: Atonement
books.author: Ian McEwan
books.synopsis: In the summer of 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis misinterprets an encounter between her sister Cecilia and the housekeeper's son Robbie Turner, then falsely accuses Robbie of a crime, sending him to prison and later to war, a lie whose consequences Briony spends the rest of her life trying to atone for as a novelist rewriting the truth.

books.title: Books: A Memoir
books.author: Larry McMurtry
books.synopsis: The novelist-turned-antiquarian-bookseller traces his life from a bookless Texas ranch childhood through decades of scouting, buying, and dealing rare books at his Georgetown and Archer City shops, Booked Up.

books.title: The Baron in the Trees
books.author: Italo Calvino
books.synopsis: After a childhood quarrel with his father, young Cosimo Piovasco di Rondò climbs into the trees of his family's Ligurian estate and vows never to set foot on the ground again, living out the rest of his life aloft while hunting, reading Enlightenment texts, corresponding with Diderot, falling for a girl named Viola, and getting drawn into the political upheavals of his era from among the branches.
